name: Face Mask Edge
description: Detects face mask edge artifacts and measures deviations from authentic physical baselines to identify AI intervention.
algorithm: Face Mask Edge — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method specifically targets the face mask edge artifacts produced by face-swap deepfakes:

1. **Face Mask Region Estimation**: The likely face mask used in the deepfake generation is estimated by analyzing the spatial extent of generated content. Face-swap models use face detection to define a mask region (typically a convex hull of landmarks or Delaunay triangulation), then blend the synthesized face within this mask.

2. **Edge Artifact Detection**: At the mask boundary, multiple artifact types are detected: (a) color seams where generated and original content don't color-match perfectly, (b) texture discontinuities from different rendering qualities, (c) double edges where mask feathering creates a visible transition zone, (d) compression artifact differences between generated and original regions.

3. **Feathering Analysis**: The mask edge feathering (smooth alpha transition) is characterized. The method measures feathering width, symmetry, and consistency. Deepfake feathering tends to be uniform width around the entire mask, while natural face boundaries have varying transition characteristics (sharp at hairline, gradual at jaw-neck junction).

4. **Mask Shape Characterization**: The inferred mask shape is analyzed. Common deepfake masks follow landmark-derived geometric shapes. The method detects unnaturally geometric or symmetric face boundaries inconsistent with natural facial contours. Specific deepfake architectures produce characteristic mask shapes that can be identified.

5. **Temporal Mask Edge Tracking**: The face mask edge position and artifact characteristics are tracked across frames. In well-executed deepfakes, the mask tracks face landmarks frame-by-frame, but the mask edge artifacts (color seams, texture mismatches) may vary in intensity — becoming more visible in challenging lighting or at extreme head poses. These temporal variations are quantified for scoring.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through face mask edge analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
